842	am I faithful to the divine essence that HaShem gave me, or am I betraying it? That is really the depth of this inquiry.

844	I need to be faithful to my own self, to my soul, to my inner self.
845	How will I know what my soul-self is?
846	Torah. Because if I look only at myself, I might find

850	feel that from myself. The Torah gives us
851	the complete view of our essence. And so faithfulness
852	to the Torah is faithfulness to myself. This is the accounting:
853	I stand in judgment and accounting before the Torah, because that is judgment and
854	accounting before my deepest, true soul-self. Avraham
855	Avinu, who was completely connected to himself, kept the whole
856	Torah from within his kidneys. We, who have lost
857	that same tamim-ness, need the Torah and the
858	mitzvot to bring us back to this original thing.
859	And so we must always be accountable
860	before the Torah and the mitzvot: where are we, and have we
861	sinned or not? Sin is a disconnection from oneself,
862	and what is my essence? It is the Torah. Therefore, unlike
863	accountings before people, the accounting for Torah and mitzvot
864	is rendered to the Master of the world. This is critical, because He truly
865	is the source of our life, and connection to Him is
866	vitality. That is the first point. Now there are
